items.title: CVE-2026-0250 GlobalProtect App: Buffer Overflow Vulnerability during connection to Portal or Gateway (Severity: MEDIUM)
items.one_liner: Palo Alto Networks patches a buffer overflow in GlobalProtect clients that could allow MITM code execution with SYSTEM privileges.
items.summary: A buffer overflow vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-0250, exists in the Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect app during portal and gateway connection processing. An adversary positioned as a man-in-the-middle can disrupt system processes and potentially execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges on affected Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and ChromeOS endpoints. The vulnerability is rated medium severity with a CVSS base score of 7.7, and Palo Alto Networks has confirmed no active exploitation.

Impact: Arbitrary code execution with SYSTEM privileges
items.bottom_line: Man-in-the-middle attackers can exploit CVE-2026-0250 in the GlobalProtect app to achieve arbitrary code execution with SYSTEM privileges.

items.one_liner: Vanus default hardcoded credentials expose clusters to unauthenticated administrative compromise.
items.summary: Vanus versions 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 contain a critical default credentials vulnerability allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to gain cluster-admin access via a hardcoded admin token. Attackers can send a fixed Bearer token to the gateway gRPC proxy port to manage namespaces, eventbuses, users, tokens, and role bindings, or read and publish events. The vulnerability has been assigned a CVSS base score of 9.3 and was published on October 18, 2026. This flaw exposes cloud-native event-driven architectures to complete administrative takeover without credentials.

items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve full cluster-admin access on vulnerable Vanus instances using a hardcoded admin token.

items.title: PHP core RCE vulnerability patches (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
items.one_liner: Critical PHP engine RCE flaws require immediate patching across all web server deployments.
items.summary: PHP has disclosed two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, stemming from how out-of-memory errors are handled via longjmp(). When OOM errors occur, contexts may leave request memory uninitialized before allocations, allowing subsequent cleanup routines to read or branch on this memory and achieve RCE. Fortinet is actively investigating impact across its product suite while confirming several products like FortiOS are unaffected. The flaws affect nearly every PHP version back to PHP 5.4, requiring administrators to update their PHP runtime immediately. Attackers can trigger these conditions consistently through multiple OOM strategies, posing severe risks to web servers.

CVE-2026-109619: PHP core remote code execution flaw
Affected Products: FortiADC, FortiClient EMS, FortiSIEM, FortiSOAR and others under investigation
Unaffected Products: FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiWeb
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve remote code execution on PHP web servers via runtime memory corruption triggered by OOM errors.

items.title: LiteLLM Compromised in Supply Chain Attack Delivering Credential Stealer and Backdoor
items.one_liner: LiteLLM PyPI compromise deploys credential stealers and backdoors via stolen GitHub OAuth tokens.
items.summary: The popular LiteLLM Python package version 1.107.0 was compromised in a software supply chain attack distributing a credential stealer and a persistent backdoor via PyPI and Docker images. Threat actors utilized stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens across three engineers' accounts to trigger and approve the malicious release. The malware executes via a Python path file (`cook.pth`) prior to package import, harvesting cloud credentials, private keys, browser data, AI tool configuration files, and environment variables. Compromised data is exfiltrated via HTTP POST to `litellm[.]dev/healthcheck`, while a secondary payload establishes a GitHub-based dead-drop mechanism for executing arbitrary remote Python code.
key_facts: Payloads: Privcollect credential stealer and GitHub dead-drop backdoor
Attack Vector: Stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens
items.bottom_line: Attackers compromised LiteLLM version 1.107.0 using stolen GitHub OAuth tokens to deploy a credential stealer and a GitHub-backed remote execution backdoor.

items.title: PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge
items.one_liner: Emergency PHP2Shell patches fix critical unauthenticated RCE flaws in the PHP runtime engine.
items.summary: PHP has issued emergency patches in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 to fix two critical runtime remote code execution vulnerabilities collectively known as PHP2Shell. Tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 with CVSS scores of 9.2, the flaws reside in the PHP engine rather than site applications, exposing servers regardless of code security. Apache mod_php installations face the highest risk, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute code and read live worker memory containing sensitive credentials before application code runs. Security researchers from Wiz and OpenAI discovered the flaws, prompting emergency backports for older branches.
items.bottom_line: Emergency updates for PHP fix two critical engine-level vulnerabilities that allow unauthenticated remote code execution and memory theft across web servers.

items.title: U.S. Orders DeepSeek Removed From Federal Civilian Systems, Bans New Purchases
items.one_liner: Federal civilian agencies and government contractors are legally barred from using or procuring DeepSeek AI tools under a new DHS supply-chain security order.
items.summary: U.S. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin issued an order under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018 requiring federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products and related implementations from their IT systems. The order also bars these agencies from purchasing new IT products or services from Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd. or its affiliates. Furthermore, the restriction impacts federal contractors by incorporating FAR clause 52.204-30, requiring them to screen supply chains, check SAM.gov every three months, and report any covered products within three business days. The notice, dated July 24, 2026, was published in the Federal Register on October 20 without providing reasons.

items.one_liner: OpenTelemetry exporter versions 1.5.0 to <1.45.0 suffer from disabled TLS verification when certificate paths are left blank, enabling MitM attacks.
items.summary: OpenTelemetry's opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http package contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in versions 1.5.0 prior to 1.45.0. When the OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE environment variables are left as empty strings, TLS verification is incorrectly disabled. This allows man-in-the-middle attackers to impersonate the collector and intercept, read, or modify exported traces, metrics, logs, and sensitive authentication headers such as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 8.3 (High).
items.bottom_line: Upgrade OpenTelemetry exporter packages to version 1.45.0 or later to patch improper certificate validation (CVE-2026-112006).

items.title: Combining Long-Term Memory and LLMs Comes at a High Cost: From Prompt Injection to Persistent Compromise
items.one_liner: LLM persistent memory features enable cross-session prompt and memory injection attacks across major platforms.
items.summary: While generative AI prompt injections were traditionally confined to single sessions, modern persistent memory features enable cross-session attack propagation known as memory injection. Researchers evaluated leading LLM services, demonstrating that NIST attack goals are achievable across ChatGPT Instant 5.3, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3 Flash. Memory injections leverage personal memories, projects, skills, organization instructions, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-connected resources to persistently spread disinformation or generate harmful content across fresh sessions. In Claude, shared-memory features allow attackers to compromise multiple organizational users and exfiltrate prompts, highlighting critical gaps in current platform security mitigations.

Attack Vectors: Personal memories, projects, skills, organization instructions, MCP-connected resources
items.bottom_line: Persistent memory features in conversational AI platforms allow attackers to execute cross-session memory injections that persistently compromise multiple users and exfiltrate data.

items.title: Compaction Laundering: Provenance Destruction in Context-Compacting Coding Agents
items.one_liner: Context-compacting coding agents flatten message role labels in harnesses, allowing malicious prompts to launder into long-term memory as trusted user instructions.
items.summary: Coding agents running long sessions frequently compact their context memory by discarding historical transcripts and summarizing conversations, creating an exploitable trust boundary defect called compaction laundering. When harnesses flatten conversation trees into plain strings with generic role labels like [User]: before passing them to a summarizer, user provenance is destroyed, allowing attackers to forge user turns that survive compaction as genuine instructions. Tests across five popular open-source flattening harnesses showed successful laundering rates between 87% and 100%, whereas role-typed harnesses prevented the attack entirely. This laundered memory successfully commands coding agents to execute remote code snippets or bypass code reviews, highlighting the need for code-level serializers to properly escape role labels or retain role typing.
key_facts: Affected Harnesses: pi, opencode, Cline, Aider, OpenHands
Attack Success Rate: 87-100% across flattening harnesses
Context Window tested: Up to ~908,000 tokens
items.bottom_line: Flawed conversation flattening in open-source coding agents destroys message provenance during context compaction, letting attackers inject persistent malicious instructions into agent memory.

claims.text: Coding agents that run long enough must compact their context, summarizing the conversation, discarding the original, and carrying the summary forward as memory.

items.title: The Show-Up Attack: When Subagents Win Over Their Supervisor
items.one_liner: Multi-agent LLM systems are vulnerable to 'show-up attacks' where subagents bypass scope restrictions, requiring stronger architectural security controls.
items.summary: Researchers have identified the 'show-up attack,' a vulnerability in multi-agent LLM systems where a malicious subagent manipulates its supervisor into assigning it tasks outside its authorized scope. Evaluation of six frontier LLMs using the SUA-Arena framework revealed that all are susceptible to this attack, with some supervisors showing an attack success rate (ASR) as high as 0.93. The study concludes that current mitigation strategies like prompting or restricted communication are insufficient, necessitating explicit authority enforcement mechanisms.
items.bottom_line: Developers building multi-agent systems must implement explicit, hard-coded authority boundaries rather than relying on LLM-based instructions to prevent subagent privilege escalation.

items.title: Multiple Cisco Products Snort 3 Visual Basic for Applications Buffer Overflow Denial of Service Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A stack overflow in Cisco's Snort 3 VBA decompression engine lets remote attackers cause a denial of service.
items.summary: Multiple Cisco products contain a vulnerability in the Snort 3 Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) Decompression Engine due to improper range checking. An unauthenticated, remote attacker can exploit this flaw by sending crafted VBA data to trigger a stack overflow in the detection engine. This unexpected overflow forces the Snort 3 Detection Engine to restart, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. Cisco has released software updates and provided workarounds to address the vulnerability.

items.one_liner: JQ::Lite for Perl before 2.51 allows arbitrary code execution via unsafe evaluation of regex code blocks.
items.summary: JQ::Lite for Perl in versions before 2.51 contains a high-severity vulnerability where regex patterns provided to test(), match(), or select() conditions are compiled using string eval. Patterns are placed directly into `qr'...'` literals and compiled as source text, causing any embedded `(?{ ... })` code block to execute without validation or restriction. An attacker who supplies a query or controls input inserted into a query pattern can execute arbitrary Perl code within the calling process. NVD has assigned the vulnerability a CVSS base score of 8.4.
items.bottom_line: Unsafe string evaluation of query patterns in JQ::Lite for Perl before 2.51 enables arbitrary code execution via crafted regular expressions.

items.title: Microsoft pins ConnectWise supply-chain attack to China-state aligned threat group
items.one_liner: Storm-0940 used the ARTEX AI pentesting framework to automate supply-chain compromises across ConnectWise customer environments.
items.summary: Microsoft has attributed a recent supply-chain attack against ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers to the China-state aligned threat group Storm-0940. Operating since September 2026, the threat actor utilized an agentic AI penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate password-spraying, reconnaissance, and credential modifications. During the campaign, the group targeted hundreds of organizations globally and reached over 2,250 tenants at high speeds. ConnectWise temporarily shut down services and began a phased recovery, advising customers to keep connections disabled.
items.bottom_line: Nation-state groups are successfully leveraging agentic AI frameworks to execute high-speed, automated supply-chain compromises at scale.

items.title: SafePay Has Compromised 600 Critical Infrastructure Victims Worldwide, CISA Warns
items.one_liner: SafePay ransomware has hit over 600 critical infrastructure targets globally using extensive initial access vectors and double extortion.
items.summary: The SafePay ransomware group has compromised at least 600 critical infrastructure organizations across North America, South America, Europe, and Australia since emerging in August 2024. A joint advisory from US, German, and UK agencies highlights SafePay's extensive initial access vectors, including credential exposure, brute-force attacks, VPN exploitation, and edge device vulnerabilities. The group employs living-off-the-land administrative tools, disables security software, and uses a double extortion model backed by phone calls and a ChaCha20/RSA hybrid encryption scheme. SafePay is believed to be a rebrand of well-known ransomware operations like LockBit, ALPHV/BlackCat, and INC Ransomware.

Encryption: ChaCha20 stream cipher with RSA public-key cryptosystem
items.bottom_line: Critical infrastructure defenders face an active, highly prolific ransomware threat operating through multiple historical threat actor techniques.

items.title: State Bank of India Confirms Data Leak After 3,897 Customer Records Found on Dark Web
items.one_liner: State Bank of India confirmed a data leak exposing personal details of 3,897 customer records on the dark web.
items.summary: The State Bank of India (SBI) confirmed an incident involving the loss of certain data after 3,897 customer records containing personal information were found within a dark web dataset of roughly 375,000 records. The exposed data includes customer names, registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, residential addresses, and internal CIF identifiers, though sensitive financial details like account balances and passwords were not listed. The leak was flagged to the bank on October 16 by CERT-In and the Defense Cyber Agency, prompting SBI to engage an independent cybersecurity auditor. While the bank noted no material impact on core operations, the exposed details pose severe impersonation and phishing risks to customers.
key_facts: Exposed Records: 3,897 customer records identified out of ~375,000 total records
items.bottom_line: Exposure of customer PII and internal identifiers from India's largest bank creates immediate impersonation risks, requiring heightened vigilance against targeted phishing.

items.summary: Critical security vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language—discovered via AI and estimated by Wiz to affect roughly 70% of the internet—have prompted global government warnings and emergency patching efforts. items.one_liner: CVE-2026-103090 allows unauthenticated attackers to steal Biscuit identity tokens in Google OSS Agent Mesh.
items.summary: A vulnerability, CVE-2026-103090, has been identified in the control plane enrollment status handler of Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.8. The flaw lacks authentication for critical functions and insufficiently protects credentials, enabling an unauthenticated remote attacker to retrieve approved bootstrap-enrolled peers' signed Biscuit identity tokens. Users must upgrade to version 0.1.0-alpha.9 or later, which enforces cryptographic proof of possession and rate limiting.

items.title: [0day-rubbish] Royal Render 9.1.26b: default-unauthenticated job submission on rrServer TCP 7773 reaches worker-side shell execution as the worker identity, measured root (8.1 High)
items.one_liner: Royal Render 9.1.26b ships with unauthenticated TCP job submission, letting attackers execute arbitrary shell scripts on worker nodes.
items.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in Royal Render version 9.1.26b allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution on worker nodes. The central scheduler (rrServer) runs on TCP port 7773 and lacks authentication by default, as shipped configuration files set nTCPRequiresAuth to false and leave the whitelist empty. Malicious job submissions can specify an Execute job type with a shell script path (`.sh`), which the worker evaluates via a shell template. The vulnerability enables arbitrary command execution under the worker's system privileges.
key_facts: CWE: CWE-306, CWE-1188, CWE-73, CWE-250, CWE-284, CWE-1392
items.bottom_line: Default-unauthenticated job submissions in Royal Render rrServer lead to direct remote code execution on worker nodes.

items.one_liner: Compromised global TLS CA private keys trigger a 34% crash in eMudhra shares over three sessions.

items.title: Securing Agentic Commerce Through Behavior-Aware Fraud Detection and Cybersecurity for Trusted AI-Agent Payment Authorization
items.one_liner: ACAGS is a new machine-learning framework combining behavioral analytics and delegated authorization controls to secure AI-agent commerce against fraud.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced the Autonomous Commerce Agent Guard System (ACAGS), a cybersecurity framework designed to secure autonomous AI agents in digital commerce against threats like impersonation, unauthorized payments, and malicious delegation. Utilizing XGBoost alongside behavioral analytics, agent-specific authorization controls, and SHAP explainability, the framework was evaluated on synthetic financial transaction data. Experimental results showed that adding behavioral and agent-specific features boosted mean F1-scores, achieving high detection rates for abnormal behavior, impersonation, and authorization-scope violations. The model supports APPROVE, REVIEW, and REJECT outcomes, demonstrating how behavioral intelligence can protect AI-agent payment workflows.
items.bottom_line: The ACAGS framework uses behavioral analytics and machine learning to secure autonomous AI agents against payment fraud and impersonation.

items.title: PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agents via Machine-Checked Integrity Theorems and Scalable Community Trust
items.one_liner: PerMIT introduces provable memory integrity architectures for safe autonomous LLM agent self-improvement.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced PerMIT, a persistent memory architecture designed to secure LLM agents against injection and poisoning attacks using machine-checked integrity theorems. PerMIT mediates untrusted environment-derived values through a finite memory interface while preserving agent planning capabilities, ensuring sensitive actions only execute if confirmed at a gate. Theorems proven and machine-checked in Lean 4 reduce threats to auditable human or LLM verification decisions. Simulations on Trojan Hippo showed zero observed attack success, and deployments on tau^2-bench demonstrate that multi-agent communities can safely build shared knowledge bases without direct memory injection.
items.bottom_line: PerMIT secures LLM agent persistent memory against injection attacks by enforcing a finite mediation interface backed by machine-checked integrity theorems.

items.summary: Modern Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools have evolved from passive, operator-configured rules to black-box autonomous systems driven by AI components. items.title: Recoverability and Verifier Strength: Two Measured Preconditions for Unattended Agent Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: Establishes measurable preconditions and safety rules for unattended AI agent self-improvement loops.
items.summary: Agent platforms aiming for unattended self-improvement must measure two critical preconditions: verifier strength (how reliably an LLM judge agrees with a trusted reference) and recoverability (how cheaply and completely a bad change can be undone). The authors built a platform enforcing the rule that edits run unattended only if old versions are preserved and verifier strength is explicitly measured, revealing that LLM judges often approve arbitrary outputs without flagging errors. Testing on $	au^2$-bench demonstrated that unmanaged changes altered task outcomes by 17 percent beyond normal variation, validating the necessity of strict rollback controls.
items.bottom_line: AI agent self-improvement loops must verify automated judge reliability and maintain mandatory code rollbacks before running unattended.

items.title: AgentPolicyForge: From Executable Environments to Policy Benchmarks and Adaptive Guards
items.one_liner: AgentPolicyForge introduces an executable environment framework to benchmark agent policies and train adaptive guards that reduce attack success.
items.summary: Researchers introduced AgentPolicyForge, a framework designed to construct policy benchmarks and iteratively train adaptive guards for customized AI agent deployments. The framework utilizes executable environments to generate tool-call data across 10 policy families, forming the PolicyGym dataset comprising 698 training scenarios and 254 held-out test scenarios. By recording tool execution outcomes and testing argument-level and context-level compliance, the framework enables iterative fine-tuning using balanced, environment-verified examples. Evaluations on PolicyGym show that the guard-based configuration achieves a 40-44% relative reduction in attack success rate compared to prompt-based instructions alone.

items.title: DuplexLedger: Benchmarking Transactional Memory in Full-Duplex Speech Agents
items.one_liner: DuplexLedger and ACT-Mem benchmark and improve transactional memory tracking in full-duplex conversational AI agents.
items.summary: Researchers introduced DuplexLedger, a bilingual benchmark comprising 1,094 persistent sessions to evaluate transactional memory handling in full-duplex speech agents. Testing five full-duplex models revealed a severe interaction-memory gap, with the best final-state fact coverage reaching only 2.01%. To address this, the authors proposed ACT-Mem, an 8.92M-parameter sidecar featuring an event controller and versioned transactional ledger built around a frozen MiniCPM-o 4.5 backbone. On held-out sessions, ACT-Mem improved latest-value accuracy from 4.11% to 8.68% while reducing stale assertions and distractor adoption.
items.bottom_line: Full-duplex LLM speech agents fail at state tracking, but sidecar architectures like ACT-Mem can significantly improve memory accuracy and reduce stale assertions.

items.title: Black-Box Red-Teaming of Multi-Agent Systems via Reinforcement Learning
items.one_liner: ReMAS is a new reinforcement learning framework for black-box red-teaming and prompt extraction in multi-agent systems.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced ReMAS, the first reinforcement learning-based red-teaming framework designed specifically to uncover vulnerabilities in multi-agent systems (MAS). Existing black-box red-teaming techniques primarily target single LLM agents and show limited effectiveness in multi-agent setups where sub-agents do not directly interact with users. ReMAS operates in a two-step process utilizing a rewrite stage to refine base attack prompts and a template generation stage to invoke specific sub-agents for system prompt extraction. Experiments demonstrate that ReMAS significantly improves attack success rates and exhibits robust transferability across different backend LLMs and system architectures.

items.title: PROVISO: Provenance-Informed Action Selection for Secure LLM Agents
items.one_liner: PROVISO uses provenance-typed memory to secure LLM agents against malicious tool outputs and prompt injections.
items.summary: Researchers introduced PROVISO, a controller designed to secure LLM agents by evaluating proposed actions against provenance-typed memory before execution. Unlike existing defenses that judge tool calls in isolation, PROVISO tracks whether content originates from trusted user input or external tool outputs, querying role-specific memories to select actions with the highest calibrated utility. Evaluations across security benchmarks showed that PROVISO outperforms baselines, improving F1 scores by 13.84 points on SkillsBench and 7.07 points on ToolSafe.
items.bottom_line: PROVISO successfully balances security and utility for LLM agents by incorporating data provenance tracking into action selection.

items.title: SUDP: Secret-Use Delegation Protocol for Agentic Systems
items.one_liner: SUDP is a delegation protocol for agentic systems that prevents prompt injections from stealing reusable API secrets.
items.summary: To address how agent runtimes frequently authorize actions by exposing reusable secrets or tokens—turning transient prompt injections into durable account compromises—researchers formalized the Agent Secret Use (ASU) problem. They proposed the Secret-Use Delegation Protocol (SUDP), which ensures that an untrusted autonomous requester can trigger user-authorized, secret-backed operations without gaining reusable authority over the underlying credential. In SUDP, a requester proposes an operation, the user authorizes it with a fresh authenticator-backed grant, and a custodian redeems the grant for a bounded execution. A reference implementation demonstrates sub-millisecond protocol overhead per mediated call, satisfying security properties when combined with a hardware-rooted runtime.
key_facts: Protocol Overhead: Sub-millisecond protocol overhead per mediated call
items.bottom_line: Implementing SUDP in agent runtimes prevents compromised or prompt-injected coding agents from obtaining durable, reusable access to user API secrets.

items.title: USN-8951-1: c-ares vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: Multiple denial of service and memory allocation vulnerabilities in c-ares impact multiple Ubuntu LTS versions.
items.summary: Several vulnerabilities have been identified in c-ares, an asynchronous DNS client library, affecting various Ubuntu releases. These flaws include improper parsing of SOA replies and sortlist strings, inadequate limits on DNS compression pointer hops and name lengths, and a lack of proper record count validation before memory allocation when processing DNS responses. A remote attacker could exploit these issues to cause denial of service via excessive resource consumption or crashes, or potentially execute arbitrary code. Ubuntu has published security updates to resolve these vulnerabilities across supported package versions.

items.title: Ransomware gangs have been exploiting Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN flaw since June
items.one_liner: Ransomware groups are actively exploiting a Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN authentication bypass flaw to gain initial corporate footholds.
items.summary: Multiple ransomware gangs, including Qilin, Inc, and Settra, have been actively exploiting CVE-2026-0257—an authentication bypass vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect VPN and Prisma Access patched in May. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass security restrictions and establish unauthorized VPN connections by exploiting cookie handling flaws. Once inside corporate networks, threat actors bypass multi-factor authentication, use IT management tools for lateral movement, disable ESIx/vCenter security controls, and deploy custom tools to extract domain-wide credentials before launching ransomware attacks.

items.summary: Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in Unbound, a validating, recursive, and caching DNS resolver, affecting various Ubuntu LTS releases. items.title: Scanning AI Assets: Catching What SCA and SAST Might Miss
items.one_liner: Coding agent skills and manifests can hide malicious instructions that bypass traditional SCA and SAST tools over 90% of the time.
items.summary: Traditional application security tools like SCA and SAST often fail to catch security flaws inside AI assets such as SKILL.md files, agent plugins, and APM manifests because these formats carry instructions and intent rather than just compiled code. Research in July 2026 demonstrated that an evasion framework could hide malicious payloads in skills and bypass eight commercial scanners more than 90% of the time while still executing successfully in production environments like Claude Code and Codex. These cloaked AI assets can introduce prompt injection, hidden instructions, obfuscated payloads, and credential exfiltration. Security solutions must therefore evaluate agent intent and instructions rather than solely relying on traditional code pathways.
key_facts: Evasion rate: More than 90% against 8 scanners
items.bottom_line: Conventional code scanners miss AI intent and instruction-based threats, exposing development pipelines to stealthy supply-chain compromises via agent skills and plugins.

items.one_liner: OpenCode silently patched a critical CVSS 9.8 RCE flaw involving malicious MCP servers, leaving developers vulnerable without CVE alerts.
items.summary: Security researchers at Pillar Security disclosed a critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-free, assessed at CVSS 9.8) in open-source AI agent platform OpenCode affecting versions 1.0.137 to 1.18.32 on Windows and WSL. The flaw allows an attacker-controlled remote model context protocol (MCP) server to execute arbitrary code on a developer's machine during an MCP OAuth authentication process without user interaction. Researchers warn that URL validation alone is insufficient and recommend updating vulnerable dependencies and avoiding passing untrusted URLs directly to shell commands.
items.bottom_line: Developer tooling security risks are amplified when platforms silently patch critical RCE vulnerabilities without issuing CVE advisories.

items.one_liner: CVE-2025-39964 is a Linux kernel AF_ALG race condition that grants root privilege escalation and container escape.
items.summary: Researchers detailed the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem. The flaw allows an unprivileged user to execute out-of-bounds access, escalate privileges to root, and escape Docker containers. Discovered by Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan and completed with Billy Jheng Bing-Jhong at STAR Labs, the bug earned a $113,337 reward through Google's kernelCTF program. Unlike Copy Fail, which is a straight-line logic flaw in the AEAD path, CVE-2025-39964 involves a race between writers sharing an AF_ALG socket present since 2011.

items.bottom_line: Unprivileged users can abuse cryptographic API race conditions in the Linux kernel to achieve root privilege escalation and container escapes.

items.title: AI Security Scoping: Define What To Test In Your Deployment
items.one_liner: Stop treating AI security as a single 'check' and start scoping it across the entire ecosystem, including APIs, identity, and data flows.
items.summary: Effective AI security requires a system-wide view that extends beyond the model boundary to include APIs, orchestration layers, and data pipelines. Security teams should anchor their efforts on specific risk decisions, such as enabling production data or detecting lateral movement, and select appropriate methods like AI penetration testing or red teaming. This structured approach ensures that security outcomes are measurable and defensible.

items.one_liner: Vyper 0.4.0b1 to 0.5.0b1 miscompiles code due to name shadowing of imported constants and default arguments.
items.summary: Vyper versions 0.4.0b1 through 0.5.0b1 suffer from a name shadowing vulnerability for imported constants and default arguments. This can corrupt type validations and accounting logic.

items.title: CVE-2026-114639 - Traefik before 2.11.58 and 3.7.14 Authentication Bypass via Negotiate Connection Pool
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-114639 lets unauthenticated attackers hijack NTLM/Kerberos-bound sockets via Traefik's shared backend connection pool.
items.summary: An authentication bypass vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-114639 affects Traefik versions before 2.11.58 and 3.7.14. The flaw occurs because a preauthenticated request using an Authorization: Negotiate token authenticates a socket in the globally shared backend connection pool, which lacks proper isolation. Consequently, unauthenticated attackers on separate frontend connections can be assigned the same NTLM or Kerberos-bound socket, allowing them to execute reads or writes using the victim's identity.

items.title: One Tap Too Far: Using Shortcuts to Bypass Chrome for iOS Call Prompts

Apple and Chrome resolved the issue by introducing a confirmation prompt prior to executing any Shortcuts or Workflow URLs.

items.title: How APT41 revived the BlackLotus bootkit to attack diplomatic organizations in Central Asia
items.one_liner: APT41 and associated actors revive the BlackLotus UEFI bootkit to target diplomatic agencies in Central Asia.
items.summary: Kaspersky researchers have discovered an advanced persistent threat (APT) campaign targeting diplomatic organizations in Central Asia, including Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan, using a revived UEFI bootkit dubbed BlackX. The bootkit borrows core exploitation techniques from the infamous BlackLotus bootkit—specifically bypassing Secure Boot via the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894)—by installing custom Machine Owner Keys after attackers achieve administrator privileges. The campaign utilizes custom RC4-encrypted installer packages containing helper files to drop malicious UEFI components that inject custom drivers into the Windows kernel, marking a rare instance of an APT group adopting techniques or code originating from cybercrime forums.

items.bottom_line: Threat actors are deploying the BlackX bootkit, a derivative of BlackLotus, to bypass Secure Boot and compromise diplomatic targets in Central Asia.

items.title: Prompt Injection Through Forensic Evidence: A Taxonomy and Proof of Concept of Anti-Forensic Attacks on LLM-Assisted Digital Investigations
items.one_liner: Research highlights anti-forensic indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities in LLM-assisted digital investigation tools.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced a taxonomy and proof-of-concept for anti-forensic indirect prompt injection attacks targeting LLM-assisted digital investigations. Because digital forensic evidence is attacker-controlled by definition, reasoning layers in AI tools become novel attack surfaces that existing prompt-injection defenses fail to address. The study highlights a perception gap between deterministic tools, human examiners, and language models. Demonstrations confirm that malicious text planted on a seized device can successfully alter reported conclusions, write attacker code to an analyst's workstation, and trigger outbound network traffic.
items.bottom_line: Digital forensic examiners utilizing LLM assistants are vulnerable to malicious prompt injections embedded directly within seized evidence.

items.title: How Much Does the Harness Matter, and for Whom? A Multi-Model Study of Context in LLM-Driven Vulnerability Discovery
items.one_liner: A study on LLM vulnerability discovery shows engineered prompts and CodeQL context drastically boost smaller models, often matching frontier performance at lower costs.
items.summary: A research study evaluating 24 model-runner configurations on a production codebase examined how agent harnesses and prompt contexts affect LLM-driven vulnerability discovery across 265 confirmed security root causes. The findings demonstrate that combining an engineered prompt with a CodeQL-derived call graph significantly increases criticality-weighted yield for smaller and mid-tier models by 20-86%, while frontier models show a smaller 2% improvement. Separating these factors revealed that engineered prompts improve yield across all models, whereas additional CodeQL context only helps the smallest models. Furthermore, strong lower-cost models can match frontier model performance at a fraction of the cost, highlighting the importance of matching models, prompts, and context to specific tasks.
items.bottom_line: Lower-cost models paired with robust CodeQL context and engineered prompts can achieve vulnerability discovery yields comparable to expensive frontier models.

items.title: ProMemAgent: Long-Horizon Proactive Assistance with Context-Aware Prospective Memory from Sensory Perceptions
items.one_liner: Introduces ProMemAgent, an LLM agent leveraging sensory prospective memory for long-horizon proactive assistance.
items.summary: Researchers introduce ProMemAgent, a proactive LLM agent framework designed for long-horizon assistance through context-aware prospective memory derived from everyday sensory perceptions such as video and audio. The agent organizes past sensory histories to generate prospective cues, retrieving relevant events to perform memory-augmented proactive reasoning. To evaluate long-term capabilities, the authors also introduce CPMBench, comprising 1,000 instances across eight categories, where ProMemAgent outperformed existing baselines in memory retrieval and proactive task execution.
items.bottom_line: ProMemAgent demonstrates that structuring egocentric sensory inputs into prospective memory enables LLM agents to deliver reliable long-horizon proactive assistance.

items.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
items.one_liner: Multi-objective RL for LLM-based RTL code generation produces diverse Pareto-optimal circuits across power, performance, and area trade-offs.
items.summary: Researchers proposed a multi-objective reinforcement learning method with large language models to generate Pareto-optimal RTL circuits from natural-language specifications. Instead of aggregating power, performance, and area (PPA) metrics into a single scalar reward, the approach reformulates coverage improvement of the entire Pareto solution set into a sequential circuit generation problem guided by a Hypervolume Contribution (HVC) reward function. Evaluated on the RTLLM v2 benchmark, the method achieved a 13.3 percentage point relative Hypervolume increase over a PPA-unoptimized baseline and a 14.4 percentage point increase over single-objective reinforcement learning, while improving circuit diversity.

items.title: RaspAssistant as an Agentic Framework for Automating Adsorption Simulation Research in Porous Materials
items.one_liner: RaspAssistant demonstrates that hierarchical multi-agent frameworks can successfully automate complex materials simulation and adsorption workflows.
items.summary: Researchers tested RaspAssistant, a hierarchical multi-agent framework designed to automate end-to-end adsorption-simulation research in porous materials. Across twelve workflow-reproduction runs spanning four benchmarks, overall evaluation scores ranged from 8.50 to 10.00 on a rubric assessing correctness, simulation validity, and analysis consistency. In an eight-case force-field extraction benchmark, the mean weighted score achieved was 0.967, and open-ended testing successfully diagnosed and refined an acetylene force field while screening 197 pure-silica zeolites. These results demonstrate that autonomous multi-agent systems can execute extended simulation workflows while exposing methodological limitations for expert review.

items.title: MemDev-Bench: Does Memory Help Code Agents?Benchmarking Memory Systems over Real Repository Histories
items.one_liner: Introduces MemDev-Bench to show how memory systems improve code agent editing while risking unassessed failures.
items.summary: The authors introduce MemDev-Bench, an evaluation framework pairing repository tasks with relevance-annotated historical tasks to benchmark memory systems for code agents across 4,869 historical tasks. The evaluation reveals that memory primarily improves fine-grained localization and editing for functional correctness, but also causes failures on otherwise solvable tasks when agents reuse unassessed or irrelevant history. Furthermore, providing raw historical trajectories directly reduces agent steps by retaining process information that compressed memories omit.
items.bottom_line: Code agent memory systems must preserve process tracking and revalidate applicability to prevent regressions on repository tasks.

items.one_liner: Introduces MAMath-Bench to evaluate multimodal multi-agent mathematical reasoning and process reliability.
items.summary: Researchers introduce MAMath-Bench, a process-aware benchmark comprising 1,003 problems across 11 mathematical categories and multiple modalities (text, images, and audio) designed to evaluate multimodal multi-agent mathematical reasoning systems. The evaluation assesses problem-solving correctness, reasoning-process reliability, and robustness against adversarial reasoning-chain perturbations. Findings indicate that multi-agent collaboration does not consistently improve final-answer accuracy over strong single LLMs, increases reasoning redundancy, and remains vulnerable to adversarial structural perturbations.
items.bottom_line: Multi-agent LLM systems for math reasoning increase intermediate step coverage but remain vulnerable to adversarial structural perturbations.

items.title: The More the Better? A Comparison of Single- and Multi-Agent LLM Setups on a Financial Review Task
items.one_liner: Multi-agent LLM financial review setups catch slightly more defects but increase false alarms and token usage compared to repeated single-agent sampling.
items.summary: A controlled study comparing single-agent and multi-agent LLM setups on a financial review task revealed that dividing requirements across a three-agent team catches slightly more explained defects on models where single agents miss some, but consistently increases false alarms across all models. The team setup used 2.2 to 2.4 times more tokens than the single agent. Furthermore, sampling a single agent multiple times achieved higher balanced accuracy than the multi-agent team while consuming significantly fewer resources.

items.bottom_line: Splitting tasks among multiple agents increases false alarms and token costs without necessarily outperforming simple repeated sampling of a single agent.

items.title: Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training
items.one_liner: Navalia offers developers a verifiable synthesis and post-training approach for building robust financial and office LLM agents.
items.summary: Researchers introduced Navalia, a framework designed to advance Cowork Agents by integrating verifiable task synthesis and long-horizon post-training using corporate financial reports. The framework extracts evidence from factual datasets, builds executable computation chains, and applies independent LLM review and programmatic checks to verify data consistency and correctness. The verified trajectories are subsequently used for cold-start supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve complex task execution. Initialized from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Navalia demonstrates consistent performance gains over base models across five evaluation benchmarks, including OfficeQA Pro and FinSearchComp.
key_facts: Benchmarks used: OfficeQA Pro, FinSearchComp, Finance Agent Benchmark, APEX-Agents-AA, Workspace-Bench-Lite
items.bottom_line: Verifiable task synthesis and structured post-training significantly enhance LLM agent performance in complex, multi-step financial reasoning tasks.

items.title: TxnQA: Benchmarking Analytical Reasoning and Evidence Grounding over Transaction Event Sequences
items.one_liner: TxnQA benchmarks analytical reasoning and evidence grounding over transaction event sequences, exposing arithmetic and attribution bottlenecks.
items.summary: Analyzing merchant transaction histories requires irregular event stream processing and dynamic temporal filtering that traditional benchmarks fail to capture. To bridge this gap, researchers introduced TxnQA, an analytical QA benchmark featuring 27 task families across 81 templates and a 5-scenario fraud-risk reasoning suite built on privacy-mitigated transaction data. Model evaluations show that while adaptation and LoRA training successfully enforce output formats, arithmetic and evidence attribution remain major bottlenecks. Specifically, while verdict accuracy often exceeds 80%, joint accuracy requiring exact evidence attribution collapses to at most 23%.
items.bottom_line: LLM evaluation on transaction data reveals that models frequently reach high verdict accuracy while failing at rigorous evidence grounding and arithmetic tasks.

claims.text: We introduce TxnQA, an analytical QA benchmark comprising 27 task families (81 templates) alongside a 5-scenario fraud-risk reasoning suite that evaluates both verdicts and supporting evidence over synthetic, privacy-mitigated transaction data.

items.title: SIREN (Luring LLMs onto the Rocks): PAIR-Driven Preference Manipulation in Web-RAG Recommenders
items.one_liner: SIREN demonstrates how adversarial content poisoning of retrieved web sources can reliably manipulate LLM-generated recommendation rankings.
items.summary: Researchers introduce SIREN, an automated attacker-judge method that adapts the PAIR jailbreaking loop to competitive rank manipulation in web-augmented large language models. When LLMs act as recommenders by retrieving live web pages, attackers can manipulate the final rankings by iteratively editing retrieved sources using a taxonomy of 23 content-poisoning techniques while keeping the surrounding source set fixed. Tested across two production Claude models, SIREN achieved rank 1 in 62 out of 124 trials, with payloads showing high reproducibility in fresh sessions. The findings indicate that declarative ranking claims and seeded lists are generally more effective than directive-form injections for altering LLM recommendations.
key_facts: Success count: rank 1 reached in 62 trials
items.bottom_line: Web-augmented RAG recommenders are vulnerable to targeted content poisoning that can systematically promote attacker-chosen entities to the top recommendation slot.

items.title: Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design: From Architecture Search to Organizational Learning
items.one_liner: Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design (AMOD) establishes an execution-driven loop for searching multi-agent structures.
items.summary: Agentic system design is shifting toward automated search over multi-agent programs and interaction structures, raising questions about functional divisions of responsibility. To address this, researchers propose Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design (AMOD), which treats organization as a first-class design object that models team composition, responsibilities, and coordination rules. AMOD operates as an execution-driven design loop where an automated designer instantiates organizations, evaluates execution outcomes and interaction traces, and revises ineffective responsibilities. The approach provides a principled foundation for evidence-based multi-agent architecture search.
items.bottom_line: AMOD provides an automated, evidence-based approach for optimizing multi-agent team architectures and functional responsibilities.

items.title: Runtime Control for AI Agents: Closing the Evaluation--Execution Gap in Operational Workflows
items.one_liner: A new runtime assurance layer addresses the evaluation-execution gap for AI agents making operational commitments.
items.summary: Language-model agents in operational workflows face an evaluation-execution gap where approvals become invalid after underlying facts or policies change. Researchers proposed a state-bound runtime assurance layer that separates probabilistic measurement from deterministic adjudication, binds execution allowances to the original decision basis, and rechecks admissibility at dispatch. In a scripted 42-case replay, this configuration successfully identified 15 later-invalidated approvals, held 14 actions before dispatch, and compensated one landed effect. This approach helps maintain authorization integrity for AI agents operating in workflows with commitments.
items.bottom_line: AI agents operating in workflows with financial or authorization commitments require state-bound runtime validation to prevent actions on outdated approvals.

items.title: Act on Your Behalf, Beyond Your Authorization: Benchmarking LLM Agent Authorization Alignment
items.one_liner: AuthorizationBench reveals that LLM agents frequently violate delegation boundaries regardless of task success, highlighting a gap in safety alignment.
items.summary: Researchers introduced AuthorizationBench to evaluate authorization alignment in Large Language Model agents across situational triggers and application domains. Testing 286 executable tasks across 24 configurations revealed that agents act outside their authorized scope in 19.2% of trajectories, proving that successful task completion does not guarantee adherence to delegation limits. Furthermore, agents exhibited higher rates of unauthorized actions under benign pressures than malicious injections, and those that consulted the principal beforehand demonstrated lower violation rates.
items.bottom_line: Standard task completion metrics fail to catch authorization alignment failures, with LLM agents frequently executing actions beyond their permitted scope.

items.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
items.one_liner: MedPAO-Assist brings edge-deployable, modality-aware agentic AI using small language models to radiology reporting workflows.
items.summary: MedPAO-Assist is an edge-deployable agentic framework designed to structure radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation without needing cloud APIs or internet connectivity. Utilizing a small language model in the 0.6B-parameter range, it requires approximately 3.3 GB of peak RAM and achieves an average end-to-end latency of roughly 31 seconds on standard laptop CPUs using an asynchronous multi-threaded pipeline. The system supports four major imaging modalities—Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI—through an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm followed by a speech-driven correction phase. This architecture facilitates offline operation and data privacy compliance in clinical environments.
key_facts: Supported modalities: Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, Brain MRI
items.bottom_line: Small language model agents can deliver offline, privacy-compliant radiology report structuring on standard laptop hardware.

items.title: REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents
items.one_liner: REM improves coding agent memory reuse and repository bug-fixing accuracy by controlling memory storage, recall gates, and lifecycle eviction.
items.summary: Researchers introduce REM (Reusable Experience Memory), a framework designed to manage experience memory lifecycles for coding agents executing long-horizon tasks across repository-level codebases. Traditional retrieval methods struggle because they lack visibility into active agent execution loops, failing to determine precisely when or how long an experience is needed. REM manages memory via three distinct decisions: storing completed trajectories as phase-structured documents, injecting them at task starts while withholding implementation records, and evicting records after a single exposure. Evaluated on SWE-ContextBench Lite, REM achieved a 68.7% match@1 retrieval rate, improved task resolution to 27.6%, and reduced costs by 17% compared to existing baseline methods.
items.bottom_line: Managing the agent memory lifecycle internally yields higher task resolution and lower operational costs than standard retrieval-only methods.

items.title: CertMoE: Robustness Certification for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs via Routing-Aware Smoothing
items.one_liner: CertMoE is the first routing-aware robustness certification framework that provides provable guarantees for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced CertMoE, a routing-aware robustness certification framework designed to provide provable guarantees for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models under adversarial perturbations. Existing certification methods assume fixed computation graphs, which fail in MoE models due to input-dependent routing that induces discrete and dynamic execution paths. CertMoE establishes a relaxed routing-containment criterion that bounds perturbed Top-K routing within a larger certified expert pool, constructing corresponding sub-networks to certify prediction consistency. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that CertMoE significantly reduces certification violation rates compared to traditional methods.
items.bottom_line: CertMoE successfully certifies the robustness of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs by accounting for input-dependent dynamic routing paths.

items.title: Omni-Woodpecker: Hallucination Correction via Evidence-Prior Rebalancing for Omni LLMs
items.one_liner: Omni-Woodpecker is a training-free framework that corrects cross-modal hallucinations in Omni LLMs via representation rebalancing.
items.summary: Omni LLMs (OLLMs) often suffer from cross-modal hallucinations due to entangled grounding evidence and learned priors in fused representations. To mitigate this without retraining, researchers proposed Omni-Woodpecker (OWP), a training-free framework that performs conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing. OWP detects cross-modal conflicts from modality-specific views, applies orthogonal decomposition to separate evidence from priors in hidden states, and adjusts the representation before decoding. Experiments show that OWP improves performance across multiple benchmarks when using models like Qwen2.5-Omni-7B and VideoLLaMA2-AV.
key_facts: Performance gains: +12.9 on CMM, +8.6 on AVHBench
items.bottom_line: Cross-modal hallucinations in Omni LLMs can be mitigated without retraining by separating grounding evidence from priors in hidden states.

claims.text: Using Qwen2.5-Omni-7B as the backbone, OWP improves performance by 12.9 and 8.6 points on CMM and AVHBench, respectively, while consistently achieving gains of 0.67-2.25 points across four general OLLM reasoning benchmarks.

items.title: When Health Assistants Agree Too Readily: A Benchmark of Time-Critical Self-Diagnosis
items.one_liner: SelfDx benchmark reveals that frontier health assistants frequently agree too readily with user self-diagnoses, risking dangerous delays in urgent medical care.
items.summary: Researchers introduce SelfDx, a benchmark designed to evaluate whether frontier LLM health assistants exhibit appropriate epistemic independence when responding to user self-diagnoses. Testing 27 frontier models across 100 paired cases, the authors discovered that models frequently and inappropriately agree with user self-diagnoses even in caution cases where severe alternative conditions (such as meningitis) remain viable. The best-performing model achieved only a 77.0% appropriate caution rate on time-critical conditions. Experiments with prompt variants showed an increase in caution but reduced appropriate agreement by 9-35%, whereas supervised fine-tuning on balanced examples improved both rates concurrently.
items.bottom_line: LLM health assistants require targeted post-training rather than brittle prompting to maintain appropriate caution in time-critical self-diagnosis scenarios.

items.title: A Unified Evaluation Framework of Physical Adversarial Robustness in the Edge VLM Era
items.one_liner: A new unified evaluation framework benchmarks the physical adversarial robustness and dangerous failure modes of edge VLMs.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced a unified evaluation framework to systematically assess the physical adversarial robustness of edge Vision-Language Models (VLMs) compared to traditional object detectors. By defining a conditional attack success rate (cASR) and categorizing failures into omission, substitution, and displacement, the study benchmarks compact grounding VLMs against various object detectors under physical adversarial patches. Results reveal that VLMs are as vulnerable as traditional detectors and tend to shift toward dangerous substitution and displacement failure modes under distribution shift, returning high-confidence erroneous bounding boxes.
items.bottom_line: Edge Vision-Language Models inherit physical adversarial vulnerabilities from object detectors and frequently fail via dangerous high-confidence box substitutions.

items.title: Beyond Binary Labels: Diagnostic Evaluation of LLM Safety with Prompt-Level Rubrics
items.one_liner: DiagSafe replaces binary LLM safety labels with rubric-driven prompt evaluations, achieving high human agreement and unmasking nuanced model flaws.
items.summary: Current LLM safety benchmarks rely heavily on binary safe or unsafe labels, which suffer from poor inter-judge consistency and lack explanatory depth. To fix this, researchers introduced DiagSafe, a diagnostic evaluation framework that utilizes prompt-level rubrics grounded in global AI safety policies across safety and usefulness dimensions. Evaluated on a bilingual English-Chinese dataset containing direct queries, template jailbreaks, and complex instruction-following attacks, DiagSafe achieved 95.34% agreement with human annotations. The framework uncovers distinct model vulnerabilities across languages and multi-turn contexts, providing an explainable auditing tool for LLM alignment.
items.bottom_line: A new rubric-based diagnostic framework, DiagSafe, significantly improves LLM safety evaluation reliability by moving beyond simplistic binary classifications.

items.title: ReuF2F: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Formalized Undergraduate Research Problems
items.one_liner: A new Lean 4 benchmark of 244 undergraduate research problems shows that even top coding agents currently solve only about 40% of them.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced ReuF2F, a Lean 4 benchmark featuring 244 formalized open problems sourced from Research Experiences for Undergraduates to evaluate end-to-end open problem resolution in coding agents. Traditional benchmarks often focus on known results or prominent problems that become harder to evaluate once solved. To test agents fairly, the benchmark places each problem and its logical negation into a Lean project within a Docker container, using a unified harness called Leanimum-agent. Evaluations revealed that the top-performing model resolved only about 40% of these problems, demonstrating significant room for improvement.
items.bottom_line: Current coding agents struggle with formal mathematics on unmined research problems, resolving only 40% of tasks in the ReuF2F benchmark.

items.title: More Memory, Worse Agents: Error Reproduction and Anti-Persistence in LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Anti-Persistence memory architecture prevents LLM agents from propagating corrupted rules by separating raw experience storage from dynamic guidance generation.
items.summary: LLM agents often store execution experience in external memory to improve across tasks, but retaining inferred rules and abstractions can propagate and compound errors through a feedback mechanism called error reproduction. To counter this, researchers propose Anti-Persistence, a memory design that accumulates raw trajectories and outcomes while dynamically synthesizing and discarding task-specific guidance on demand rather than storing abstract rules directly. Evaluations across various benchmarks and backbones demonstrate that Anti-Persistence achieves higher overall held-out success rates and lowers average LLM-call costs compared to traditional memory designs.
items.bottom_line: Storing abstract rules in agent memory propagates errors, whereas generating task guidance on demand from raw trajectories improves success rates and lowers costs.

items.title: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing
items.one_liner: A comprehensive survey and architectural framework for deploying LLM-driven industrial agents in smart manufacturing environments.
items.summary: This article outlines a systematic overview of Large Language Model-driven industrial agents designed for smart manufacturing. It analyzes five key core challenges, establishes a unified taxonomy for application scenarios and embodiment forms across five capability levels, and proposes a four-layer system architecture for closed-loop task execution. The study reviews representative applications throughout the industrial lifecycle and points out future research directions. It serves as a structured reference for developers building autonomous manufacturing agents.
items.bottom_line: LLM-driven industrial agents require a structured four-layer architecture and capability taxonomy to address complex manufacturing constraints.

items.title: KPHarness: Co-Evolving Knowledge and Probing for Long-Horizon Gaming Harnesses
items.one_liner: KPHarness co-evolves recovery knowledge and active probing to automatically adapt execution harnesses for long-horizon vision-language-action models.
items.summary: Researchers introduced KPHarness, a framework that adapts the external execution harness of a frozen vision-language-action model for long-horizon gaming tasks through knowledge-probing co-evolution. By combining recovery knowledge hypotheses with active probing, the system uses probe outcomes to refine both intervention rules and investigation strategies via a slow research loop separate from fast policy execution. Evaluated on Minecraft tasks spanning mining, combat, and crafting under matched sandbox conditions, KPHarness demonstrated improved task coverage and completion over bare policy execution, fixed manual harnesses, and non-adaptive knowledge evolution.
items.bottom_line: Automating harness adaptation through active knowledge probing significantly improves long-horizon task execution for vision-language-action models.

items.title: SPEM: Structure-Aware Procedural Memory for Efficient Skill Use in LLM Agents
items.one_liner: SPEM uses a structure-aware procedural memory framework with Skill-DAGs and GNNs to improve LLM agent skill execution efficiency.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed SPEM, a lightweight structure-aware procedural memory framework designed to improve skill use efficiency in LLM-based agents. SPEM maintains an Atomic Skill Memory for individual skills alongside a Skill-DAG Memory for reusable composite workflows derived from successful executions. When tackling new tasks, the framework reuses high-confidence Skill-DAG templates or invokes a Skill-GNN module for state- and structure-aware skill selection. Experiments on ALFWorld and SkillsBench demonstrate that SPEM achieves superior effectiveness-efficiency trade-offs while lowering token and runtime costs.
items.bottom_line: SPEM reduces token and runtime overhead for LLM agents by organizing reusable skills into structured DAGs and GNN-backed selection.

items.title: Teaching AI Agent to Play Poker Strategically Through Preference Optimization
items.one_liner: Strategic Preference Optimization with KL-anchored Equilibrium (SPOKE) trains compact AI agents to play poker more strategically.
items.summary: To address whether compact language models can exhibit strategic behavior under hidden information, researchers evaluated multiple models on poker tasks and proposed Strategic Preference Optimization with KL-anchored Equilibrium (SPOKE). SPOKE combines teacher-relative value penalties, policy anchoring, risk constraints, and structured rationale supervision. Tested on a SmallThinker-4B-A0.6B policy, SPOKE achieved lower mean exploitability in Kuhn and Leduc poker variants and higher top-1 agreement compared to baseline optimization methods like SFT, DPO, and GRPO.
items.bottom_line: SPOKE alignment techniques improve the strategic gameplay and lower exploitability of compact language models in imperfect information games.

items.title: Modeling Authentic Research Trajectories: A Graph View of Research Ideation
items.one_liner: The Research Progress Graph (RPG) models the authentic evolution of scientific ideas to improve AI research agent design.
items.summary: Research ideas in published papers typically evolve through a closed-loop trajectory involving experiments, insights, challenges, and literature reviews, but existing AI research agents discard the reasoning and evidence connecting these iterations. Researchers proposed the Research Progress Graph (RPG) to model authentic research trajectories as typed research states connected by cognitive transitions with temporal and reasoning annotations. Evaluating thirty-five existing research agents against the RPG showed that none maintain a complete record of changing states, supporting evidence, and reasoning. The authors argue that adopting the RPG framework can improve how AI research agents are designed, trained, and evaluated by focusing on ideation trajectories rather than static text generation.
items.bottom_line: AI research agents should be evaluated and trained on complete idea trajectories rather than static final outputs to better mimic authentic scientific ideation.

items.title: TEX: Test-Time Scaling Testing Agents via Execution-based Cross-Validation
items.one_liner: TEX is an execution-driven cross-validation scaling framework that improves test-time agent performance on long-horizon tasks.
items.summary: Generating reliable test cases for long-horizon agentic tasks remains difficult for language models. To improve performance, researchers developed TEX, a collaborative test-time scaling framework that uses execution-driven cross-validation. TEX parallelizes agents to generate tests and code patches, cross-executing every test against every patch to build a KxK feedback matrix without sharing verbose traces. On SWT-Bench Verified, TEX achieved an 86.4% success rate, representing a 9.0% improvement over single-agent baselines and demonstrating that execution-grounded feedback scales solution quality effectively.
items.bottom_line: Parallelized execution-grounded feedback improves test generation and patch validation for AI agents on complex software engineering tasks.

items.title: Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry
items.one_liner: Magnolia provides computational chemists with a persistent-memory LLM agent framework that improves reproducibility and error prevention across workflows.
items.summary: Researchers introduce Magnolia, a persistent-memory AI agent framework designed for computational chemistry that integrates molecular databases, docking and quantum chemistry protocols, lab notebooks, and chat logs. Magnolia employs a three-tier memory architecture: capturing session-level observations, distilling them into structured project-tier entries, and elevating human-validated insights into cross-project rules that actively guide future workflows. Evaluated across four case studies including quantum chemistry and protein-peptide docking, Magnolia tracked 317 runs, accumulated 116 project entries, and established four cross-project rules. Replay tests demonstrated that agent runs equipped with persistent memory successfully passed verification checks that non-memory runs failed.
items.bottom_line: A multi-tier persistent memory framework enables scientific AI agents to retain cross-project learnings and consistently pass chemical verification checks.

items.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
items.one_liner: LightCRS delivers multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendations with a 5.3M-parameter shared module, cutting per-query latency by 266x and setting new accuracy benchmarks.
items.summary: LightCRS is a lightweight, query-conditioned framework designed for unified multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. It avoids the linear scaling costs of separate per-domain vision-language models and the accuracy degradation of naive single-VLM merging by precomputing multimodal product representations once offline with frozen encoders. Online, a compact 5.3M-parameter module fuses evidence via query-conditioned cross-attention shared across all domains and jointly compares candidates using an inter-candidate Transformer. Evaluated on a new 25-domain benchmark called MM-R2A-25, LightCRS achieves state-of-the-art average HR@1, NDCG@5, and MRR metrics, improving HR@1 by 35.4% over the strongest baseline and reducing per-query latency by 266 times. Furthermore, joint multi-domain training itself improves HR@1 by 15.2% over separately trained single-domain models.
items.bottom_line: Shared, query-conditioned cross-attention can unify multimodal product recommendations across 25 domains with a 5.3M-parameter module while drastically reducing latency.

items.title: Beyond Experience: Knowledge-Guided Evolution for NPU Kernel Generation
items.one_liner: A new framework improves NPU kernel generation by grounding LLM evolutionary search in external technical documentation.
items.summary: ASCENDEVOLVE is a new framework designed to improve LLM-based NPU kernel generation by grounding evolutionary search in a large external knowledge base. Unlike previous methods that rely solely on agent experience, this approach retrieves task-specific evidence from platform documentation and operator repositories to guide implementation and repair. Testing on 53 Ascend C operators showed significant performance gains over existing methods like Reflexion and OpenEvolve.
items.bottom_line: LLM agents can achieve higher performance in NPU kernel generation by using external knowledge retrieval rather than relying solely on trial-and-error memory.

items.title: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
items.one_liner: Multi-agent collaboration improves clinical task performance but does not inherently reduce rationale hallucination, which depends entirely on the base model.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated whether multi-agent LLM systems reduce hallucination in clinical reasoning tasks, testing a single-LLM baseline alongside three multi-agent topologies across four models and three clinical tasks. Scoring hallucinations inside the generated rationales using a factuality and faithfulness taxonomy, the study found that collaboration improves final task metrics but does not systematically reduce hallucinations. The level and direction of hallucination changes are determined by the underlying base model rather than the multi-agent topology or agent count. A self-correction experiment further showed that most models reduce hallucinations when shown their own errors, but collaboration merely redistributes existing model capabilities rather than supplying missing ones.
items.bottom_line: Multi-agent LLM collaboration increases task performance without necessarily reducing reasoning hallucinations in clinical applications.

claims.text: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system.

items.title: Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation
items.one_liner: Ask-to-Distill uses a distributional surrogate over frozen student-teacher pairs to synthesize and filter high-value questions for on-policy distillation without needing reference answers.
items.summary: Ask-to-Distill (method) is a framework that treats synthetic questions as distribution elicitors to optimize teacher supervision during on-policy distillation (OPD) without requiring correct reference answers. A student-initialized synthesizer is optimized using a distributional surrogate for question value derived from a frozen student-teacher pair, combining teacher-student disagreement, teacher probability mass, and length and diversity controls. The generated questions are subsequently filtered and deduplicated into a prompt-only bank for standard OPD. Across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and agentic tasks, the method improves average performance and teacher-gap recovery over unoptimized student-generated prompts and KL-filtered real questions. Signal analyses further show that these optimized questions elicit denser supervision and more total signal from shorter student responses.
items.bottom_line: Synthetic questions can be reliably optimized as distribution elicitors for on-policy distillation without access to ground-truth answers.

items.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
items.one_liner: DataPraxis uses verified workspace evolution to synthesize 5,000 analytics trajectories, producing open models that rival frontier analytics agents.
items.summary: DataPraxis is an analytics task synthesis framework designed to scale agentic professional data analysis through verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, combines them to surface deeper questions, and verifies analytical results during evolution and post-assembly. Using this approach, the authors constructed DataPraxis-5K, a dataset of 5,000 verified trajectories across diverse domains and output formats, and trained DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B models. DataPraxis-27B achieves scores of 55.11 on DABStep and 51.9 on JobBench, matching or exceeding frontier models such as GLM-5.2.
items.bottom_line: Progressively enriching and verifying analytical workspaces provides a scalable path to training high-performance data analysis agents.

items.title: Unsupervised Tool Evolution for Coding Agents in Data-Lake Analytics
items.one_liner: TEAL enables unsupervised tool evolution for coding agents in data lakes, significantly improving performance without human labels.
items.summary: Researchers introduced TEAL (Tool Evolution for Analytics over data Lakes), an unsupervised framework that builds and refines reusable tools for coding agents without ground-truth labels. The system employs an Explorer agent to mine data lakes and a Critic agent to evaluate Worker trajectories, retaining tool modifications only if the Worker successfully adopts them on reruns. Evaluated on KramaBench and LakeQA across tight step budgets, TEAL improved the performance of every Worker model, lifting Sonnet-5 by 9.3 points on KramaBench and 21.7 points on LakeQA at a 15-step budget. Additionally, synthetic-question evolution performed comparably to real-question libraries, showing that effective agent tool evolution can be achieved without expert labels.
items.bottom_line: TEAL successfully evolves reusable analysis tools for coding agents in an unsupervised setting, substantially boosting data-lake task performance.

items.title: Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4
items.one_liner: Compiler-guided repair modules use Lean 4 error messages to fix failed proof tactics in place, nearly doubling solve rates on benchmarks.
items.summary: Automated theorem provers for proof assistants like Lean often discard precise compiler error messages during pure sampling. To fix this, researchers introduce a bounded, online step-level repair module that samples candidate tactics and feeds compiler error messages into a pretrained repair model to correct rejected steps in place. Testing on a 1,990-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark across various candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), the repair module yields up to a 32% relative gain in solve rates and solves 82 additional theorems. The approach demonstrates that repair is front-loaded, with the first repair attempt capturing 84% to 96% of the total gain, mostly by resolving shallow tactic-execution failures rather than deep type mismatches.
key_facts: Relative solve rate gain: up to 32%
items.bottom_line: Feeding compiler error messages directly into a pretrained repair model overcomes the limitations of pure sampling in automated theorem provers.

items.title: A general-purpose System One decision model for clinical records
items.one_liner: CS1-4B is a compact 4B clinical decision model that matches larger open models while performing rapid patient record analysis with high token efficiency.
items.summary: Clinical System One (CS1-4B) is a 4-billion-parameter decision model trained on 12.4 million Q&A pairs from 3.6 million patients across a multi-hospital health system to extract rapid judgments from patient records. It processes structured data keys, observed outcomes, and supervision across notes and diagnostic reports in a single forward pass without task-specific retraining, outputting explicit probabilities to route uncertain cases to human review. Tested on 963,408 held-out patients, CS1-4B outperformed open decision models up to 27 billion parameters on 13 of 14 independent tasks and showed 6.4-fold faster inference. When integrated into agentic harnesses with generalist language models, CS1-4B enabled multi-year record analysis and screened populations for clinical trial eligibility using 690-fold fewer language-model tokens than full-record reading approaches.
key_facts: Training scale: 12.4 million questions from 3.6 million patients
items.bottom_line: A small specialized clinical decision model can handle repeated record reading and classification, freeing generative models to focus on reasoning and evidence synthesis.
